case_name: Matadin and Others v State of Uttar Pradesh
respondent:
State of Uttar Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

6 March 1979
Cr.A. No. 120 of 1973.
The Judgement was delivered by: FAZAL ALI, J.
1. In the appeal u/s. 2(a) of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, the appellants have been convicted u/s. 302 read with S. 149 and sentenced to imprisonment for life. They have also been convicted u/s. 148 IPC and sentenced to one year R.I. They are further convicted u/s. 324 read with S. 149 for which they have been sentenced to two years R.I. The sentences have been directed to run concurrently. All the appellants were acquitted by the learned Sessions Judge but the High Court on appeal by the State convicted them of the various charges mentioned above.

facts: In the appeal u/s. 2(a) of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, the appellants have been convicted u/s. 302 read with S. 149 and sentenced to imprisonment for life.
All the appellants were acquitted by the learned Sessions Judge but the High Court on appeal by the State convicted them of the various charges mentioned above.
The occurrence took place in broad daylight and three of the eye-witnesses were injured witnesses.
Their presence at the spot cannot be doubted. There was sufficient light and in this light these witnesses could see the occurrence.
issues: Whether the evidence of the eye witnesses should be rejected
Whether the Sessions Judge's reasons for disbelieving the witnesses are good or sound
petitioner_arguments: The appellants argued that the Sessions Judge's reasons for disbelieving the witnesses were wrong, unconvincing and unsound
court_reasoning: We find ourselves in complete agreement with the judgement of the High Court.
Nothing was shown to us in the statements of the eye-witnesses by the learned counsel for the respondents on account of which their statements may be rejected.
The occurrence took place in broad daylight and three of the eye-witnesses were injured witnesses.
holding: The appeal fails and accordingly dismissed
The appellants who are on bail, will now surrender to serve out the remaining portion of their sentence
